## Outcome and scope
Deliver one complete hybrid chat workspace: existing CLI/PTY terminal plus ONE resizable side pane (browser, viewer or agents), bidirectional screenshot/file handoff, authenticated chat-local CLI/MCP pane control, and trustworthy live subagent activity. Existing run/ticket/Kanban authority and human approval boundaries remain unchanged. User-authorized checkpoint replan: deliver an independently verified accepted-core increment in Sprint1, then resolve terminal image links, final documentation and complete-product validation in Sprint2. No final feature or quality requirement is waived.

## Architecture decisions (implementation contract)
- Main owns pane resources, files, authentication and capture. Renderer owns layout/controls and sends bounded geometry via guarded typed IPC. A native browser receives no app preload/bridge. One side-pane slot per chat; hidden chats never leave native views over the active screen.
- Persist only validated per-chat layout and reopenable descriptors. Tokens, grants, socket addresses, WebContents IDs and live process state are never persisted as layout. Restore files by fresh authorization, not by reviving a token; missing temp files show an explicit missing-file state.
- Images are files in the validated chat's private staging directory under system temp, PNG/JPEG only, <=10 MiB and <=8000 pixels/side. Reuse the already-landed attachment intake/path helpers, not the old plan's conditional duplicate parser. Attachments remain durable evidence owned by the existing attachment subsystem; staging cleanup must never delete copied evidence.
- Browser uses a main-owned sandboxed WebContentsView and stable per-folder isolated session partition. Allow only http/https navigations, including localhost; deny app/custom/file schemes, permission grants and downloads. Renderer chrome, dialogs and overlays must not be occluded by the native view.
- Pane control uses the existing command table/authz plus a versioned local pipe/socket. The server derives repository/chat/session scope from a currently valid grant main bound to a live PTY, never from caller-supplied chat IDs. An arbitrary external orchestrator grant is not a desktop-chat grant. Every privileged operation revalidates authorization at execution, not just connection time.
- Capture is an actual rendered-pixels operation, not a DOM mock. Native child views and DIP/device-pixel conversions must be handled. Whole-window capture must include the native browser where shown. Background-chat requests must not silently screenshot the foreground chat or steal focus: a nonvisible pixel surface yields a defined pane_not_visible error; opening records state without switching chats.
- Activity is an observational, versioned provider adapter over actual CLI artifacts. Unknown/unsupported/stale states are visible; no invented tokens, finish status, effort or final report. Provider-derived ticket matches are advisory, never authorization or attempt evidence. Original conditional Codex adapter scope is retained: DM-466 must resolve support truthfully and implement the adapter when usable source is demonstrated, rather than treating a closure note as success.

## Two-sprint execution and standards (user-authorized replan)
- Two explicitly scoped sprints, each with a human checkpoint. Sprint1 verifies the13accepted core work items and the recorded failure/decomposition boundary; Sprint2 verifies the DM454 investigation contract, three bounded recovery implementations, final DM460 docs and the full original complete-product matrix. Dependency rows are not additional checkpoints.
- Preserve the existing standards: no mandatory tests-first and no Fireguard run. Each implementation worker writes/runs the behavioral tests listed in its ticket plus lint/typecheck for changed code; no full-suite, coverage or build sweep per ticket. Do not defer unit coverage of a ticket's risky logic to an unnamed later worker.
- Each acceptance node owns the unchanged six project DoD checks once on its combined increment, never per implementation ticket. DM449 verifies the Sprint1 accepted-core scope with current isolated/native core witnesses; DM516 verifies completed Sprint2 plus ALL original final Electron/packaged Windows/macOS,1x/non1x,clipboard/protocol/pixel/security/provider/CLI/MCP/docs and latency journeys. Recheck affected failures after repair, not full gates after every worker.
- Every required work ticket has an acceptance-node covers criterion in its assigned sprint. Record actual commands, environments/provider versions and PNG attachments. Missing external credentials/runtime are unmet gates where required. The user moved complete-product proof to final Sprint2, not out of the epic; no fixture, scaling override or accepted-core checkpoint substitutes for that matrix.
- Workers use isolated worktrees for overlapping files; serialize shared App/IPC/bootstrap/contracts when needed. Preserve unrelated user changes and the13unchanged accepted tickets. Independently review every new attempt. Only a person approves either checkpoint; original rejections are never recast as accepted.

## Non-goals
No evidence-store replacement, annotation editor, inline terminal image protocol, browser tabs or simultaneous multiple side panes. No SDK migration, executing provider transcript content, provider login bypass, elevated permissions, arbitrary file preview or automatic ticket acceptance.

## Corrected baseline and threat boundary
The image-attachments epic is complete; dm-attachment:, intake/root helpers and production CSP support already exist. xterm already has URL/OSC8/clipboard/grapheme addons; preserve them. Existing TerminalSessions.paste schedules Enter, so it cannot satisfy no-submit image handoff unchanged. chatStore.ts remains persistence owner with chatRecords.ts as facade; both layers participate. Windows named-pipe default ACLs are not a user-exclusive transport guarantee. Viewer roots intentionally retain repository/worktrees, system temp and screenshot eligibility; chat-local control is not a promise that eligible temp files are private between chats. Whole-window agent capture is opt-in, while direct human capture remains available.

Insert pasted and dropped image references without submitting or restarting the CLI. Required accepted predecessors: DM-451. This ticket is part of ONE sprint; dependency rows are not human checkpoints.

## Technical guidance and failure semantics
Do NOT call TerminalSessions.paste unchanged: writePastes schedules Enter and paste may start/resume a CLI. Add a distinct insert-without-submit operation to TerminalSessions and its injected facade, explicitly requiring an already-live ChatRef and terminal generation. Reuse safe bracketed-paste framing/queue discipline but never enqueue an Enter, kickoff flag, resume or start. Preserve every existing kickoff/Kick-back submit path and its timings.
Add guarded image intake IPC accepting either main-read clipboard or bounded renderer image bytes, never raw local file paths from a drop. Text wins when text and images coexist. Enforce per-image limits before copy, at most 20 images per gesture and 20 MiB aggregate; validate/save the whole ordered batch before a single text insertion. A validation failure types nothing and removes this batch's staging outputs.
Claim image-only paste synchronously (preventDefault before awaiting IPC), then perform clipboard lookup/save asynchronously. The xterm key callback is synchronous; do not await clipboardHasImage inside it. Coordinate native macOS Edit paste with DOM/xterm paste so a gesture is processed once, while normal text and OSC52 clipboard behavior stay unchanged. Windows/Linux no-menu behavior must remain supported.
Define one file-reference formatter shared with DM-459: escaped quoted absolute path plus a trailing space, no control characters/newlines, intended as literal CLI prompt text rather than a shell command. Capture the original folder/chat/terminal generation before any async operation; revalidate before file publication/insertion. A switched, stopped, restarted or deleted target refuses with a visible reason; never redirect to the newly active chat or restart it.

Unsupported/unverified branch: provide bounded, reproducible inspection evidence identifying executable/source versions and exact missing association/lifecycle facts; return unsupported only when that capability absence is established, otherwise not_verified/partial/unavailable as appropriate. Render the precise state through the common pane. Missing auth/CLI access does NOT prove Codex records nothing, and a successful fixture parse alone does not prove live discovery.
Keep all outcomes in this sprint. If usable records were demonstrated, implementing only an unsupported message cannot pass. If contract cannot be demonstrated, do not invent an adapter or reduce required Claude behavior. Autonomous/OMP/Cursor/custom adapters remain outside original scope; their honest support states are owned by DM-462/464. Live provider claims require observed CLI association, not Desktop rollout existence. Targeted tests plus lint/typecheck when code changes.
